person.persName: ابن العربي, محي الدين ابو عبد الله محمد بن علي بن محمد بن العربي الحاطمي الطائي
Ibn al-ʻArabī, Muḥyī al-Dīn Abū ʻAbd Allāh Muḥammad b. ʻAlī b. Muḥammad b. al-ʻArabī al-Ḥātimī al-Ṭā'ī
person.floruit: 7th / 13th century (d. 1240)Ibn al-‘Arabī was certainly the most prolific of all Ṣūfī writers; although Brockelmann (I, 571-82, S I, 791-802) lists no less than 239 works (perhaps with some duplication of works with differing titles), he himself did not know how many works he had written. The greatest influences in spreading his teaching were the works of his disciple Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī [q.v.] and Ṣadr al-Dīn’s conventicle at Konya, where there foregathered learned ṣūfīs who —many of them in flight before the Mongols—had come to Anatolia. The most important of these was the poet ʿIrāqī ([q.v.]; d. 686/1287), author of the Lamaʿāt : this abridged paraphrase in Persian of the Fuṣūṣ carried Ibn al-ʿArabī’s teaching as far as eastern Iran. Other was Saʿd al-Dīn al-Farġānī
